OpenAI launches Health in ChatGPT

Health is a new mode in which the chatbot gains access to your medical records and Apple Watch data to answer health-related questions based on your actual metrics.

Users can connect Apple Health along with medical records from hospital systems, One Medical, or Function Health. Once linked, ChatGPT can view lab results, medications, recent doctor visits, sleep, and activity data. It can compare a new blood test with previous ones, explain unclear terms from discharge summaries, or even recommend restaurants while taking allergies into account.

According to OpenAI’s own statistics, 300 million people already ask ChatGPT about health every week. Among early testers, 70% of these conversations began outside a dedicated medical section. For this reason, the relevant context is now pulled directly into regular chats without the need to switch modes.

Dedicated models have been assigned to the feature. Free users get access to GPT-5.5 Instant, which has improved recognition of situations that require a real doctor. Paid users receive GPT-5.6 Sol, which handles complex cases more accurately and explains lab results more effectively.
Data from medical records and Apple Health is not used for model training or advertising targeting. It is stored with additional encryption, can be disconnected at any time, and synchronized records are deleted within 30 days.

The feature is currently available only in the United States, on web and iOS, for users aged 18 and older on the Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans. It is not available in Codex.

📌 Rehypothecation: When One Collateral Base Works Twice

Main Points
⏺ In DeFi, the same collateral can indirectly back multiple obligations
⏺ It boosts capital efficiency but increases systemic fragility
⏺ This post explains how “leverage on top of leverage” forms

1️⃣ How It Happens — you post collateral, borrow against it, then reuse the borrowed asset as collateral elsewhere.
2️⃣ Why People Do It — yield strategies and capital efficiency: more output from the same base.
3️⃣ Where Risk Lives — a price drop can trigger cascading liquidations across layers.
4️⃣ Why It Matters — calm markets hide the links; stress markets push correlations toward 1.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — count how many collateral layers your strategy has and model a sharp drawdown.

Final Thoughts

Rehypothecation is an accelerator. It adds efficiency, but it makes systems brittle when markets break.

Here’s the breakdown on why this is a potential game-changer, especially for new pools:

The Arbitrage Engine Is Already Running

Let's talk about that brand-new pool you just saw launch. How does it earn anything on day one? The answer is simple: Arbitrage.

The moment a pool goes live, its price can slightly differ from the prices on major centralized exchanges (CEX). Smart traders and automated bots, known as arbitrageurs, are constantly scanning for these tiny gaps. They buy where it’s cheap and sell where it’s dear.

This isn't theoretical volume. Even today, with only a handful of live pools on Gala Swap, millions of dollars in arbitrage volume are flowing through the platform daily. Every single one of those trades pays a fee to the liquidity provider (LP).

Real Volume, Real Fees (Not "Farm Token" Emissions)

This is what makes Gala Swap different. The yield isn't based on inflationary "farm token" emissions that you have to constantly race against.

The LP rewards on Gala Swap are generated by real trading activity—the essential work of keeping the DEX price in sync with the broader market. When you provide liquidity, you become the infrastructure that makes this flow possible, and you earn your share of the fees from that volume.

The Real Gold Rush: Expanding the Surface

The current volume is impressive, but here’s what’s truly exciting: the bottleneck isn't the demand from traders; it's the surface area available for the arbitrage engine to work across.

A few dozen pools can only capture a few dozen tokens' worth of flow. Imagine this same efficient arbitrage engine running across hundreds of pools that simply don't exist yet.

🕴 Trump’s Press Dinner: First Amendment on Stage, Authoritarian Reflex in the Script

Donald Trump just turned the White House correspondents’ dinner into a live demonstration of how you gut press freedom while pretending to celebrate it.

This was the rescheduled, scaled‑down dinner after the April gunman incident, with fewer than 700 people, heavy security and a ballroom full of reporters who’ve spent years documenting Trump’s wars on the media. 

Instead of the usual self‑deprecating routine, he delivered more than an hour of insult comedy with almost no comedy in it: comparing a female CNN reporter to a transgender influencer, ridiculing politicians’ bodies, and declaring “I hate some people” before riffing on Adam Schiff’s “watermelon head” and “pencil neck.” 

The room mostly sat in stunned silence — not out of respect, but out of professional obligation to keep poker faces while being personally mocked.

Then he capped it by whipping out a red “Trump 2028” hat and announcing another run.

Outgoing WHCA president Weijia Jiang closed by saying “this night is all about the First Amendment.” Trump had spent it attacking the very journalists whose work makes that line meaningful. 

He mocked Kaitlan Collins. He took shots at a Wall Street Journal team that exposed his links to Jeffrey Epstein. 

He greeted a New York Times reporter who had just been subpoenaed by his Justice Department over Air Force One security reporting. 

At the same time, he insisted he wasn’t “after journalists,” only “leakers” and “cowards” whose identities he wants to extract through reporters’ records.

Trump wants the right to weaponize leak investigations against journalists who publish inconvenient truths, then show up at a dinner built on the illusion of mutual respect and call it a First Amendment celebration.

He’s already threatened to strip broadcast licenses from networks that didn’t carry his prime‑time speech on “election integrity.” He demands loyalty in coverage and punishes outlets that defy him. Associated Press was bounced for refusing to rename the Gulf of Mexico to “Gulf of America.” 

Even the setting is symbolic: the Waldorf Astoria, once Trump’s own DC hotel, now hosting a dinner where the press pretends everything is still part of a proud tradition while the president openly suggests he’ll only return if they rename it the “Trump White House Correspondents’ Dinner.” 

If you strip away the tuxedos, the magic act, and the beef tenderloin gag about Bobby Kennedy “running over the cow,” the evening tells one simple story. 

A president who calls the event “fricking stupid” and the audience “the largest group of Trump derangement syndrome people ever put together” still wants the stage, the cameras, and the aura of democratic ritual.  

His administration works to make aggressive reporting on him a legally risky profession.

🔔 Ethereum price faces $2,000 test as oil surge revives rate fears 

⚡️ Ethereum price has remained trapped below $2,000 as rising oil prices, renewed interest-rate concerns and BitMEX’s planned shutdown have tempered bullish sentiment despite continued spot ETF inflows. According to data from cryptonews, Ethereum price traded near $1,927 on July 23 after reaching an intraday high of $1,941. The token has recovered more than 27% from its June low near $1,514, but repeated failures around $1,955 have kept the psychological $2,000 level beyond buyers’ reach.

🔗 Rate traders have already adjusted their positions. The probability of a September Fed hike rose to 79% from 68% per data from the CME FedWatch tool. Expectations for the July meeting remain centered on no change, but another oil-led inflation increase could lift Treasury yields and pressure risk assets such as Ethereum. 

🔖 U.S. equities also weakened after Alphabet raised its 2026 capital-spending forecast to between $195 billion and $205 billion. The company recorded negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion as quarterly expenditure doubled to $44.9 billion, while its shares fell in premarket trading.
